newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Fed's Blinder--GDP data should raise questions.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed's Blinder--GDP data should raise questions.

text.p: Data showing a surprisingly U.S. gross domestic product growth rate of 4.7 percent for the fourth quarter should put Federal Reserve policy makers on alert, Former Fed Vice Chairman Alan Blinder said Friday.
Still, speaking in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, said the central bank should hold interest rates steady for now.
"A number that strong has got to raise eyebrows," said Blinder, who was interviewed from Davos, Switzerland, where he was attending an economic forum. The interview was monitored in Washington.
The Fed's policymaking arm, the Federal Open Market Committee, meets on Feb. 4-5 to discuss interest rates.

Asked what he would do if he were still on the FOMC, Blinder replied, "I think I would be strongly inclined to hold things as they are but would start to get a little nervous with GDP growth that strong."
"A number like that makes you think about the momentum going into the first quarter," he said.
Blinder said the Fed could be compelled to raise interest rates if growth were to continue at the fourth-quarter pace but he said he did not think that was likely.
"This last GDP number ... was well above the sustainable level," Blinder said but added that he expected growth in 1997 to be in line with the long-run sustainable trend.

Turning to the dollar, Blinder said he did not see a strong likelihood that U.S. monetary authorities would take action in currency markets to curb its recent rise against the yen, given that it was not to long ago they were contending with excessive weakness in the dollar.

"We've had some indications -- some mixed indications -- that at least some people in Japan are uncomfortable (with the dollar's rise against the yen) already," Blinder said. "We haven't had any indication of that with the U.S. authorities and I wouldn't expect one very soon."
